headline_phrase: Vitamin B12 deficiency in older adults produces neuropsychiatric presentations that are readily mistaken for primary psychiatric illness.
claim: Review of the neuropsychiatric manifestations of vitamin B12 deficiency in elderly patients, covering presentation, diagnosis and treatment.
journal: The Journal of Neuropsychiatry and Clinical Neurosciences
citation: Lachner C, Steinle NI, Regenold WT. The Neuropsychiatry of Vitamin B12 Deficiency in Elderly Patients. J Neuropsychiatry Clin Neurosci. 2012;24(1):5-15.
notes: Metadata verified against Crossref. Narrative review, so it summarizes the literature rather than testing anything.

headline_phrase: Frank folate deficiency has been under 1% of the US population since fortification. The often-quoted 20% figure is folate insufficiency in women of childbearing age, defined by neural tube defect risk, not by any mental health threshold.
claim: Folate deficiency (serum <7 nmol/L or RBC <305 nmol/L) was under 1% in persons aged 3 and over in every NHANES cycle from 1999 to 2016. Folate insufficiency (RBC <748 nmol/L, a neural tube defect risk threshold applied to women) was 18.6% in women aged 12 to 49 in 2011-2016 and 23.2% in 2007-2010.
population: US population, NHANES 1999-2016; insufficiency figures are women aged 12-49
n: 23684 serum and 24150 RBC samples in 2011-2016, ages 1 and over
journal: The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition
citation: Pfeiffer CM, Sternberg MR, Zhang M, Fazili Z, Storandt RJ, Crider KS. Folate status in the US population 20 y after the introduction of folic acid fortification. Am J Clin Nutr. 2019;110(5):1088-1097.
notes: Verified against the full text. The paper discusses neural tube defects only and contains no discussion of neuropsychiatric outcomes. Do not cite it as evidence that folate status affects mental health.

headline_phrase: Serum B12 alone misses deficiency. Methylmalonic acid and holotranscobalamin detect it earlier, which matters because the neurological damage can be irreversible.
claim: Review of the causes of B12 deficiency and of early diagnosis, arguing that holotranscobalamin and methylmalonic acid outperform total serum B12.
population: Adults, with attention to elderly, vegetarians and people with gastrointestinal disease
citation: Herrmann W, Obeid R. Causes and early diagnosis of vitamin B12 deficiency. Dtsch Arztebl Int. 2008;105(40):680-685.
notes: Verified. Sometimes cited as evidence that subclinical B12 deficiency has neuropsychiatric consequences. It is actually a review of causes and diagnosis, and supports the testing claim well and the neuropsychiatric claim only in passing.
